distinguishing_features: Detects lubricant viscosity/compressibility change via hydraulic-circuit pressure oscillation resonance shift, not bearing natural-frequency vibration shift
Uses active piezoelectric excitation of a resonator chamber rather than passive spectral analysis of existing vibration RMS
Extracts viscosity change from the K/ρ-dependent resonance frequency and damping ratio of a fluid circuit
Single-grease-drying indicator preceding mechanical backlash, using an added hydraulic resonator chamber
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Provide earlier detection of lubricant (grease) degradation before it manifests as mechanical backlash, by monitoring a fluid property that changes prior to loss of film/stiffness.
parsed.viable_reason: As written it is internally inconsistent and physically implausible: grease does not fill a 10 cc hydraulic circuit as a fluid column, an excitation of 1 kHz is orders of magnitude above the stated 5.2 Hz resonance and cannot probe it, and the stated 50 cc volume conflicts with the 10 cc design point, so the test cannot validate the mechanism.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The resonance-shift-of-a-hydraulic-circuit approach to gauge lubricant viscosity/compressibility is a distinct mechanism not suggested by the vibration-frequency-shift or static-ΔP prior art, even though using resonance to track fluid property changes is generally known.
